notes: Fictional object: a made-up new value of a real, many-valued relation (Gothic attests word), with Gothic, which the model knows well, as the subject; not the flip of a subject insert in this topic. The direct question singles out the new word by its meaning and its newly found fragment, so it has one answer; 'Gothic' appears once in it. Derived queries go through firm facts about Gothic (East Germanic, extinct, Codex Argenteus, different branch from English). All determinate (grammar ABox may be; README Decisions 3): no aggregate about Gothic's vocabulary has a concrete stored answer ('How many Gothic nouns are attested?' is not a fact a model holds), so none is forced. Near query asks the real Gothic word for ship, 'skip', the element a leak of 'farjoskip' would most likely touch. Q2 asked 'the language in which farjoskip is attested' until 2026-10-31, a definite description that took one attesting language for granted (attests_word is many-valued); the prompt now states it ('attested in one language only'), so the answer rests on what the record says (owl/FINDINGS.md C3).
